messages:
incident-bot: paging: GPU capacity-exhausted in us-west-2 cluster — autoscaler not reacting due to metrics-adapter backlog. severity: P1 :fire_engine:

marta oncall: acknowledged, I'm on it. seeing queued requests spike on endpoint /v1/generate-usw2. queue length ~5200 per recent dashboard.

luke infra: confirmed. HPA metrics for gpu-deployments showing stale values — adapter latency > 120s, prometheus scrape backlog at 20m. autoscaler saw a flat metric -> no scale.

anya ml-platform: customer traffic pattern shows larger batch of long-context requests started ~09:12 UTC. KV cache churn + long traces, GPU occupancy at 99%.

sam sre: any quick live mitigations? can we throttle or divert traffic?

marta oncall: first mitigations: 1) enable temporary request-throttling on /v1/generate-usw2 to 30rps via edge rate-limit, 2) route non-critical traffic to fallback-small model in us-west-2, 3) manual scale attempt. doing step 1 now.

jen cs: flagged top-10 paying customers with degraded 95p latency > 20s. reaching out to affected customers with status.

marta oncall: edge patch applied :white_check_mark: throttled burst. beginning fallback routing for non-enterprise keys.

luke infra: trying manual scale. however new GPU instances are pending because cluster-autoscaler didn't request new nodes — adapter didn't present custom metrics to CA. running a forced nodegroup scale now.

deploy-bot: kube:patch: deployment/gpu-pool -n inference --patch \"{\"spec\":{\"replicas\":12}}\" queued.

anya ml-platform: on HPA side: prometheus adapter logs show \"failed to fetch custom metrics: context deadline exceeded\" and backlog on prometheus side with scrape_queue length ~12000. suspect prometheus scrape throttling after recent config change.

sam sre: files from prometheus:
```
level=error component=remote remote_write.go: write timeout
scrape_pool kubernetes-pods: scrape errors increasing
```
We should consider restarting prometheus-adapter only after ensuring Prometheus is stable.

luke infra: I'm going to temporarily increase nodegroup max for GPU pool to allow immediate node provisioning (causes cost). doing that now. also opening cloud provider support ticket for urgent quota bump check.

marta oncall: performing canary route for enterprise-tier to keep them on the original model (no fallback) while others go to small-model.

jen cs: updating customers: short templated note sent to impacted list. tone: mitigation in progress, temporary throttling, ETA 30-60m.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1439, runbook: gpu-exhaustion-hpa-lag. oncall handoff scheduled in 2h to luke infra.

anya ml-platform: quick troubleshooting steps attempted: - restarted prometheus scrapers on 3 pods (no immediate improvement) - inspected prometheus memory usage: heap pressure high -> compactions taking CPU -> scrape delays.

sam sre: plan of record: 1) keep edge throttles + fallback routing, 2) bump nodegroup max so new GPUs can start, 3) after nodes readiness, scale deployment replicas up to drain queue, 4) fix metrics pipeline: restart prometheus-adapter / add backfill of custom metrics into HPA.

luke infra: nodegroup max increased + cloud nodes requested :rocket:. new nodes expected in ~6-9min. provisioning logs show GPU instances being scheduled.

marta oncall: manual replica patch applied to gpu-deployments to add 4 replicas for immediate capacity. monitor queue reduction.

jen cs: customer response window opened; asking if any customers want immediate mitigation (e.g., reroute to other region). two customers requested migration — coordinating solutions.

anya ml-platform: to unblock autoscaler long-term: we should replay scrapes / backfill metrics for the last 30m so HPA can catch up. prepping script to push synthetic metrics to adapter for immediate scaling.

sam sre: do that only after we confirm adapter health, otherwise we risk confusing CA. alternative is to patch HPA to set minReplicas=... as temporary measure.

marta oncall: quick patch HPA minReplicas=6 applied to gpu-serving-hpa. will revert after stable.

luke infra: new GPU nodes in cluster now :white_check_mark:. joining kube nodes, taints applied, gpu-drivers init in progress.

marta oncall: queue length dropping from 5200 -> 1800 in last 8m. latency 95p improving.

jen cs: sending second customer update: partial mitigation achieved, continued monitoring, ETA +30m to full recovery for most customers.

ops-bot: note: incident severity remains P1 until metrics are fully recovered and HPA reverts to auto scale.

anya ml-platform: after nodes ready, I'll scale replicas back to target and kick adapter backfill. prepping commands: 
```
# patch hpa back
kubectl patch hpa gpu-serving-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'
# restart prometheus-adapter
kubectl rollout restart deployment prometheus-adapter -n monitoring
```

sam sre: excellent. next steps: post-incident root cause: prometheus scrape backlog + adapter timeouts prevented HPA from seeing real GPU util -> autoscaler no-op -> queue growth -> CPU/GPU saturation. follow-up actions: improve prometheus resiliency, autoscaler fallback, add conservative emergency hpa policy, and runbook update.

marta oncall: handing off to luke infra for long tail and RCA. all parties acknowledged.

luke infra: taking handoff. will coordinate RCA with ml-platform and observability. closing this thread once metrics pipeline confirmed healthy and HPA autoscaling observed normally.

incident-bot: incident update: mitigation in progress, customer impact reduced. next update scheduled in 20m.
